name: Turing universal computing machine
description: A mathematical model of computation in which one universal machine can interpret an encoded description of another machine.

impact.note: Read mainly by logicians and computer scientists, but it gave a new idea of computation on which computer science and several neighbouring fields later stood.

date.label: 12 November 1936
date.basis: Date or stated historical interval in cited source; see caveats.

events.statement: Turing’s paper on computable numbers was read to the London Mathematical Society and described a universal computing machine.

evidence.supports: Manuscript read 12 November 1936 defines a universal computing machine and demonstrates limits of mechanical decision.

events.caveats: The paper identifies the reading date; the complete paper’s publication sequence is distinct. This is an abstract construction, not a working physical computer. The paper’s header records the reading, but does not establish who read it aloud.

evidence.supports: Manuscript read 12 November 1936 defines a universal computing machine and demonstrates limits of mechanical decision.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest dated witness established by the cited source for this scoped record, not a claim of global first.

caveats: The paper uses its own circle-free and symbol-printing problems; do not conflate these without argument with the modern halting problem.

research.note: Initial sourced research; independent review pending. Independent reader checked the paper’s read date and narrowed the author contribution to development; the header does not name the reader.
